# Hands-on lab authoring

- Keep the numbered exercise/task format. This companion track is not a set of fantasy adventures.
- Audit each existing lab and its actual fixtures before changing instructions.
- Use current official GitHub/Microsoft sources; cite a real verification date.
- Explain concepts, examples, use cases, concrete checkpoints, negative cases, and safe reset.
- Use Ask for investigation, Plan for design, and Agent for an approved bounded change.
- Do not infer feature status or available models from historical screenshots.
- Do not require public repositories, remote uploads, or real secrets for local learning.
- Prepare fixtures outside the curriculum root; keep caches and temporary files on the selected work drive.
- Build/test one project at a time. Never run profiling or load tests across the shared computer.
- Separate greenfield, brownfield feature work, and modernization. Modernization requires characterization tests, data validation, rollback, and explicit compatibility evidence.
- Every Mermaid block uses the repository monochrome theme, an accessible title/description, a legend, and a prose explanation.
